Subject: Assertion matrix & sampling plan for ISO/FedRAMP audit

Hi Susan / Tim —

Thanks for the kickoff earlier. Attached is the first pass of the assertion/control matrix scoped to the FedRAMP controls we discussed plus the ISO 27001 annex mapping (assertion_matrix_v1.xlsx). I also put together a short CSV with the initial sample candidates we want you to review (sample_list_request.csv).

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm the auditor sampling minimums you expect for evidence that covers both FedRAMP moderate and the overlapping ISO controls?
- Review the proposed sample candidates and flag anything that would be problematic to surface during a pre-audit (privileged access logs, PII redaction artifacts, third-party attestations).
- Let us know if CloudPartner needs any additional vendor evidence ahead of the audit window.

Target timeline: we are trying to lock samples and control owners by EOD 14 May so the audit team has a stable intake by the 18 May dry run.

Attachments: assertion_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix), sample_list_request.csv (candidates), scope-diagram.png

Thanks — I know this is tight. Karthik / Olga: please weigh in on sample feasibility and retention windows.

—Priya

From: Susan Evans <susan.evans@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Assertion matrix & sampling plan for ISO/FedRAMP audit

Priya —

Thanks for the files. Quick read-through, and a couple of clarifying questions before we lock samples:

1) Sampling minima: for FedRAMP moderate we typically expect at least 5 unique evidence items per control family when there are system-generated records (logs, configs). For managerial controls we accept fewer (2–3) provided we have documented compensating controls.

2) Scope note: Your scope-diagram.png shows a couple of 3P integrations (CloudPartner storage + analytics vendor). We will need current SOC 2 or equivalent certs from those vendors and the most recent penetration test report (redacted is fine).

3) Redaction: you called out privileged session logs as samples — we need a sanitized export for review. Can you produce a hashed or redacted sample line item for those logs?

I can confirm the auditor team can accept the matrix format; Tim, can you confirm the minimum numbers above and we will mark any exceptions in the auditor intake sheet?

- Susan
Susan Evans
Principal Security Assessor — Acme Security
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Susan Evans <susan.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Assertion matrix & sampling plan for ISO/FedRAMP audit

Susan —

Thanks, noted. Quick responses inline: 

1) Sampling minima: we can hit the 5-per-control guidance for system logs and configs for most control families. The tricky areas are:
  - Backup verification artifacts (we have snapshots but full retention policy extracts take ~48 hours to assemble)
  - Third-party certs (we have current SOC 2 for CloudPartner but the analytics vendor rotated their report last quarter — Olga, can you confirm we have the latest?)

2) Redaction: yes, we can produce a hashed export for privileged session logs. Olga will run a scrub and produce a one-page example by EOD today.

3) Timeboxing: to meet Priya's timeline we propose the following sampling allocation:
  - 60% system-generated evidence (logs, config snapshots, KV cache retention samples)
  - 25% process artifacts (runbooks, change approvals, backlog tickets)
  - 15% third-party attestations / contracts

I'll also add SOC 2 control IDs into column G of the matrix so auditors can cross-walk quickly.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance Operations | Redwood Inference

Looping in timeline/ops detail —

We can commit to the sample assembly schedule if we prioritize the owners below and limit the first intake to the control families that have the largest auditor ROI (CM, IA, SI, CP). Proposed owners:
- CM (Change Mgmt): Rohan / DevOps (will provide change tickets + approvals)
- IA (Access): Security Ops (privileged logs + SSO config)
- SI (System Integrity): Runtime engineering (binaries/build artifacts)
- CP (Contingency/Backup): Infra (snapshot retention + restore tests)

Action item for owners: upload the sample artifacts to the Drive folder linked below and add a short note (what the artifact is, date range, redaction notes). If an owner cannot meet the EOD 14 May cut, escalate to me and I'll reassign.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-assertion-matrix

—Marissa
